To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transverse rectes abdominis muscle flap and fasciocutaneus flap are good reconstructive procedures in patients with locally advanced breast cancer, with good results in terms of survival and quality of life.

the surgical closure of chest wall with transverse rectus abdominalis myocutaneous flap or fasciocutaneous flaps is a good option in patients with extended noninflammatory locally advance breast cancer with ulcerative lesion, and that quality of life has improved.
transverse rectes‐abdominis and fasciocutaneus flaps can be successfully used for reconstruction after radical mastectomy in patients with noninflamatory extended locally advanced breast carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of patients with extended locally advance breast cancer.
the best method to reconstruct the chest wall in patients with locally advanced breast carcinoma with ulceration of breast skin.
the surgical treatment of patients with locally advanced noninflammatory breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ablative surgery is appropriate in patients with extended noninflammatory locally advance breast cancer with ulcerations of the skin or muscle or infiltration of the parietal wall, who have not responded to neo‐adjuvants treatments or are not candidates for them, and in those patients who have local recurrences after mastectomy or breast conservative treatment.
in selected cases, ablative surgery with plastic reconstruction of the thoracic wall is a good option to achieve an acceptable quality of life.
ablative surgery and plastic reconstruction are a good treatment choice in patients with extended noninflammatory locally breast cancer with ulcerated skin or muscle infiltration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ablative surgery is a good option for the treatment of the disease, with a good cosmetic result.
ablative surgery is a good option for the treatment of extended locally advanced breast cancers, with acceptable survival rates and a high rate of patients without evidence of disease.

in patients who are not eligible for neo‐adjuvants or in patients who do not respond to a neoadjuvant treatment, the best procedure for reconstructive surgery of the chest wall is the transverse rectum‐abdominis flap.
The main takeaway from our work is that

reconstructive surgery is not a cosmetic procedure, but it is an integral part of the multidisciplinary approach in the treatment of locally advanced breast cancer, with the aim of improving quality of life.
patients with extended locally breast cancer can be treated with ablative surgery with acceptable morbidity.
patients who undergo reconstructive surgery for chest wall closure after radical mastectomy for extended locally advanced breast carcinoma have a good quality of life and acceptable survival periods.
